the new bombesin analogue RM2 is a potent GRPr-targeted antagonist that can be labelled with 111In for SPECT and 68Ga for PET imaging.
the new bombesin analogue RM2 is a potent and selective GRPr antagonist with high and specific uptake and retention in tumour and pancreas.
a novel bombesin antagonist was synthesized, radiolabeled and evaluated in vivo for targeting prostate cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a potent DTPA-conjugated bombsein antagonist for targeting GRP-positive tumours.
the development of a new class of radiolabelled antagonists for targeting GRPr-expressing tumours.
a new bombesin antagonist that is a potent and highly specific ligand for the GRPr and is suitable for radiometal labelling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antagonist RM2 is a potent ligand for GRPr-positive tumour imaging.
the results of this study indicate that the new DOTA-bombesin antagonist RM2 is a potent and promising candidate for further clinical evaluation in prostate cancer patients.
the bombesin antagonist 68Ga-Rm2 is a promising candidate for PET imaging of GRP receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RM2 has a very good affinity for the GRP-receptor (IC50 = 9.3 nm), and that RM2 is a good candidate for further studies.
the DOTA-antibody conjugate RM2 is a potent and promising radiotracer for targeting GRPr-expressing tumours.
the DOTA-conjugate of the bombesin antagonist RM2 is a potent and selective GRPr antagonist, with high uptake and retention in GRPr-positive tumour models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bombesin-based radiotracers are a very promising class of radiotracers for imaging GRP receptors in cancer patients.
the DOTA conjugation strategy is a promising approach to develop new GRPr antagonists for imaging and therapy of GRPr-positive cancers.
bombesin-based antagonists may have a higher clinical potential than agonists.
